# Consumer onboarding

Onboarding a new consumer team is the most frequently repeated task a Terraform platform team performs. If each onboarding is a manual set of clicks, the platform team becomes a bottleneck, configuration drifts between teams, and naming and access conventions erode. We recommend treating onboarding as a product: a version-controlled landing zone that the platform team applies for every new team, using the <a href="https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/tfe/latest/docs" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise (`tfe`) provider</a>.

This page applies to both HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise. It assumes that you have already made the organization, project, and access decisions in [Organizing resources](/validated-designs/terraform/administration-guide/organizing-resources) and configured SSO as described in [Identity and access management](/validated-designs/terraform/administration-guide/identity-and-access-management).

## Build the landing zone as code

Create an administrative project, owned by the platform team, whose workspaces manage every other project. Authenticate those workspaces with a team API token from a dedicated service-account team, stored in a variable set (`TFE_TOKEN`, and `TFE_HOSTNAME` for Terraform Enterprise). Publish reusable modules for the landing zone to the private registry, for example a project module and a workspace module, so that every team receives the same structure.

A landing zone module for one consumer team typically creates the following:

| Object | Notes |
|---|---|
| Teams | One team per role (for example admin, write, read), named to match the IdP groups and with the IdP group ID set as the SSO team ID where required. |
| Project | Named according to your naming convention, with team access granted at project level. |
| Variable sets | Provider credentials or dynamic credential configuration scoped to the project, plus common values such as cost center and owner. |
| Workspaces | Initial workspaces per environment, with VCS connection, working directory, execution mode, and agent pool assignment. |
| Policy sets | Project-scoped policy sets in addition to global guardrails. |
| Notifications | Routed to the team's group mailbox or chat channel rather than to individuals. |

Other providers can extend the landing zone: an IdP provider can create the groups, and a VCS provider can create repositories from templates, so that a single change request produces everything a team needs.

You can expose the landing zone itself as a no-code module so that project administrators request new workspaces through a form, while the platform team keeps control of the module that defines them.

## Onboarding runbook

The landing zone automates most of the work. The runbook for a new consumer team is:

1. **Collect the request.** Record the team name, application, environments, target clouds and accounts, VCS organization and repositories, and whether the team needs access to private networks.
1. **Create the IdP groups.** Follow your naming convention and group prefix so that the groups are included in the SAML assertion.
1. **Apply the landing zone.** Add the team's definition to the administrative project's configuration and merge the change. The run creates the teams, project, variable sets, workspaces, and policy set attachments.
1. **Grant VCS access.** Make sure the VCS connection can see the team's repositories; for a GitHub App installed on selected repositories, add the new repositories explicitly.
1. **Assign agent pools where required.** If the team deploys to private networks, allow its workspaces to use the agent pool for that environment, and confirm that the pool's identity has rights to the team's target environment.
1. **Validate.** Ask a team member to sign in through SSO and confirm that they land in the right teams and see only their project. Run a speculative plan in one workspace, confirm that credentials work, and confirm that policy checks run.
1. **Hand over.** Share the naming convention document, the variable precedence rules, the run workflow your organization supports, and where to get help.

## Validate onboarding at scale

Review onboarded projects periodically for drift from the landing zone, for example teams with organization-level permissions they do not need, credential variable sets attached globally, or workspaces created outside the landing zone. Because the landing zone is code, fixing drift is a change to the module or to the team's definition, applied across all teams in the same way.
